jamie (eng-runtime): Heads up — after the 02:15 canary rollout (rollout-tag=v2.3.14) we're seeing a spike in 5xx for /v1/generate and /v1/chat, ~6-9% higher between 02:18-02:31.
oncall-bot: ALERT: Anomaly detected — 5xx rate for route /v1/generate rose by 7.8% (02:19). Links: https://console.redwood/alerts/AL-9832 :rotating_light:
devon (support): multiple customers opened tickets: timeouts + partial responses, one mentions duplicate billing tokens being consumed. Customer IDs: C-9982, C-7721.
linh (sre): Can you confirm what changed in the canary? config flags, routing, or kernel selection?
jamie (eng-runtime): We flipped route-weighting to use 'new-router' (flag rollout.router_v2 = true) and increased its weight to 20% for the canary. No kernel changes.
linh (sre): 20% is higher than our usual start. Can you paste the canary ID and recent logs? Also call traces for 502/504.
jamie (eng-runtime): Canary ID: canary-2026-03-17-0215
Logs (excerpt):
```
[02:20:07] proxy: route new-router -> backend-batch-1 timeout after 3s
[02:20:07] backend-batch-1: connection pool exhausted, queued reqs=62
[02:20:09] auth: token validation error: downstream 502
```
tyler (infra): Looks like pool exhaustion on backend-batch-1. Did the canary service have mis-set connection limits?
jamie (eng-runtime): We used the same instance type but a new deploy replaced sidecar config — suspect keepalive / max-conns got reset.
devon (support): Customer C-9982 provided curl repro:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' --max-time 8
# gets HTTP 504 after 8s
```
linh (sre): Repro is consistent. Action: reduce canary traffic to 0% and roll back the router_v2 flag. Can someone execute rollback now?
jamie (eng-runtime): I'm rolling back the flag and scaling canary down.
jamie (eng-runtime): `orchctl set-flag rollout.router_v2=false --target canary-2026-03-17-0215`
oncall-bot: ACTION: Flag rollback requested by jamie (eng-runtime) at 02:35. Noted in incident: INC-4192.
tyler (infra): Also bumped backend-batch-1 pool limits and restarted pods: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/backend-batch -l shard=1`
linh (sre): After rollback & restart — monitoring shows 5xx back to baseline within ~8 mins. Confirming metrics: 02:43 5xx 2.1% -> 02:51 0.9% (baseline ~0.8%).
devon (support): Notified affected customers, issued credits for extra token usage. Will update tickets C-9982, C-7721.
jamie (eng-runtime): Root cause: new-router relied on updated sidecar connection settings that didn't land in canary images — allowed greedy connections and exhausted pool, cascading 502/504.
linh (sre): Postmortem action items:
- add canary guardrail: default traffic <=5% unless manual override (OWNER approval) :white_check_mark:
- fail deploy if sidecar config checksum mismatch :warning:
- add synthetic smoke that hits /v1/generate at canary weight to detect pool exhaustion earlier
- update runbook to include `kubectl get ep` checks for connection saturation
tyler (infra): I'll open infra PR to enforce connection limits and add the smoke test.
devon (support): I'll follow up with customers and attach RCA once draft is ready.
jamie (eng-runtime): Thanks team. I'm adding a short patch to the rollout script to prevent accidental >5% weights.
linh (sre): Closing incident channel once RCA posted. Good triage and rollback — clean comms. :thumbsup:
